about: Turning SAP's kilos into rolls and belts. SAP holds finished-goods stock as a total weight; a rep orders rolls and belts. The conversion needs two per-item numbers, weight-per-roll and belts-per-roll, and both apps must convert identically or the same shelf reads differently on a phone and a dashboard.
why: The FG catalogue import of 10 September 2026 put 1,656 items on the site, 153 with belt data and 129 holding 23,962.589 kg. It left custom_avg_weight_per_roll at 0 on all 153, breaking the site's own invariant (weight-per-belt x belts-per-roll = weight-per-roll), and 288 further items hold 37,260 kg in SAP with no belt data at all - stock that becomes eligible to land in ERPNext on the next scheduled sync.
the_trap: Frappe stores Int and Float as NOT NULL DEFAULT 0. There is no null. An item nobody has entered weights for reads exactly like an item that genuinely weighs zero per roll. Every guard here exists because those two must never be conflated: dividing by the first gives Infinity, and rendering it as 0 tells a rep 'out of stock' when the truth is 'nobody has told us how to convert this'.

rules.unknown_not_zero: A missing weight-per-roll or belts-per-roll makes the conversion UNKNOWN. Never zero, never Infinity, never a guess. The conversion's own answer is 'unknown', and it stays that way.
rules.unknown_reads_as_nothing_available: What the SCREENS do with an unknown, decided 17 September 2026 and NOT a change to the rule above. An item whose weights are not set reports NOTHING AVAILABLE - it cannot be promised - and says 'weights not set' rather than 'none left'. The two are different sentences: one is the office's problem and the other is the warehouse's. 250 of 369 stocked items are in this state today and the weights are being uploaded for the rest of the catalogue, so this is a holding position, not a design. The conversion still refuses to guess; the flag (known / weightsKnown) is what keeps the refusal distinguishable from a genuine zero.
rules.never_divide_unguarded: kg / 0 is Infinity in both languages, and Infinity rendered into an order screen is an order for an unbounded quantity.
rules.derive_weight_per_belt: weight-per-belt = weight-per-roll / belts-per-roll when the stored weight-per-belt is missing. The stored field is authoritative when present; this only fills a hole.
rules.only_weighed_units: Roll and belt maths applies to weight-based stock only. An item sold in Nos or Litre has no rolls and the question is not asked of it.
rules.whole_units_only: Rolls and belts are whole numbers. A rep cannot sell 0.885 of a roll, and a screen showing one invites an order for it. The kilos are converted to whole BELTS first, then split into rolls and the loose belts left over - which is how the stock physically sits and how the rest of the app already counts it.
rules.round_down_never_up: Always floor. 149.2 kg at 6.4 kg/belt is 23.3 belts, which is 23 sellable belts and a 2 kg offcut. Rounding to 24 promises a belt that cannot be cut, and an over-promise here is a rep standing in a shop unable to deliver.
rules.belts_first_then_rolls: Whole belts come first, then rolls = belts / belts-per-roll and the remainder is loose. Computing rolls first and multiplying back compounds the rounding error by belts-per-roll, which reaches 20 in this catalogue.
rules.float_epsilon: 34.0 / 1.7 is 19.999999999999996 in both languages, and flooring that gives 19 rather than 20 - one whole roll lost to binary floating point. A tiny epsilon is added before flooring.

cases.why: I-11672 as imported - the worked example from the brief
I-11675, the widest roll in the import
stock present, no weights - the 288 items whose SAP stock is about to land. Not zero rolls, which would read as out of stock
belts known but roll weight missing - still unknown, and still no division
roll weight known but belts missing - a roll count is derivable, but belts are not, so the pair is unknown rather than half-answered
no stock and full weights is a known zero, not an unknown - the difference between an empty shelf and an unanswerable question
a negative weight-per-roll is nonsense data, refused rather than propagated as a negative roll count
